title: Running city game optimizer: a game-based metaheuristic optimization algorithm for global optimization
abstract: Abstract As science and technology improve, more and more complex global optimization difficulties arise in real-life situations. Finding the most perfect approximation and optimal solution using conventional numerical methods is intractable. Metaheuristic optimization approaches may be effective in achieving powerful global optimal solutions for these complex global optimization situations. Therefore, this paper proposes a new game-based algorithm called the running city game optimizer (RCGO), which mimics the game participant’s activity of playing the running city game. The RCGO is mathematically established by three newfangled search strategies: siege, defensive, and eliminated selection. The performance of the proposed RCGO algorithm in optimization is comprehensively evaluated on a set of 76 benchmark problems and 8 engineering optimization scenarios. Statistical and comparative results show that RCGO is more competitive with other state-of-the-art competing approaches in terms of solution quality and convergence efficiency, which stems from a proper balance between exploration and exploitation. Additionally, in the case of engineering optimization scenarios, the proposed RCGO is able to deliver superior fitting and occasionally competitive outcomes in optimization applications. Thus, the proposed RCGO is a viable optimization tool to easily and efficiently handle various optimization problems.
venue: Journal of Computational Design and Engineering Oxford University Press (OUP)

title: CSGO: A Game-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Global Optimization
venue: 2023 International Conference on Circuit Power and Computing Technologies (ICCPCT) IEEE

title: MOA: Morabaraba Optimization Algorithm, a socio-game-inspired metaheuristic for global optimization
abstract: This paper presents a new, robust and efficient metaheuristic optimization algorithm, called the Morabaraba Optimization Algorithm (MOA), for solving unconstrained global optimization problems. The inspiration for the proposed algorithm is the traditional Southern African strategy board game Morabaraba (also known as Twelve Men&apos;s Morris), in which two teams of cows are placed, moved and flown across a 24-point board, and three aligned teammates form a mill that shoots a cow off the opposing team. MOA translates this game-play into a population-based search in which selection pressure is driven by the structural alignment of agents along board lines, rather than by fitness rank alone, complemented by a cow-count state machine that maps the game&apos;s placing, moving and flying phases onto the exploration–exploitation life cycle. The algorithm is parameter-free beyond population size and iteration budget. The MATLAB implementation, together with a 50-function benchmark library and a ready-to-run demonstration script, is described, and its behaviour is illustrated on ten representative benchmark functions, on which the software attains the known global optimum to machine precision on the majority of problems. A comprehensive experimental comparison against fifteen state-of-the-art algorithms, with non-parametric statistical testing, is reported in the companion research article [24].
